papers.title: Topological flat bands from nonlinear periodic motion
papers.abstract: We use the Lax formulation of classical integrable systems to characterize the topology of nonlinear periodic orbits. For a Hamiltonian system with one degree of freedom, we express the chiral-symmetric Lax operator along a periodic orbit in a frequency basis. Energy conservation makes both bands of the resulting tight-binding model exactly flat. The harmonic oscillator corresponds to a fully dimerized topological Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model, while nonlinearity generates long-range hopping through higher harmonics. In the symmetric double well, the winding number changes as intrawell periodic orbits give way to an orbit spanning both wells, and the zero-energy edge mode of the semi-infinite chain disappears. We derive the edge-mode profile and show that its localization length diverges logarithmically as the separatrix is approached. At the separatrix, the period and the hopping decay length diverge while the band gap remains finite; this singular limit of the periodic motion allows the winding number of the infinite frequency chain to change. Canonical quantization of the Lax operator also connects the chiral winding numbers to supersymmetric quantum mechanics: for a bound system on the real line with simple turning points, their sum over all periodic orbits at a common positive energy equals the Witten index. We also apply the construction to periodic nonlinear waves through traveling-wave reductions. The finite-period winding number becomes undefined in their solitary-wave limits.

papers.title: Lyapunov spectrum scaling transition for quasiperiodic nonlinear unitaries
papers.abstract: We study the Lyapunov spectrum scaling of thermal weakly-nonlinear unitary maps in the presence of quasiperiodic potentials. We search for the crossover from long-range to short-range scaling as the localization length {\xi} decreases and compare the details to the case of uncorrelated Anderson disorder [Phys. Rev. Res. 6 L012064 (2024)]. A comparative statistical analysis of the eigenstates for the linear case shows that quasiperiodicity has a stronger localization impact at the same value of {\xi}. Therefore we expect that the scaling crossover should be enhanced as well. However, the numerical analysis shows that it is strongly delayed as compared to Anderson disorder, and is observed at anomalously small values of {\xi}. These findings hint at the potential impact of long range correlations of quasiperiodic localized eigenstates, which persist in the presence of interactions even in the case of integrability breaking and thermalization.

papers.title: Unified Ott--Antonsen Framework for Stability and Bifurcations in Ring Swarmalators
papers.abstract: Swarmalators, a prototypical model that integrates temporal rhythms with spatial swarming, have been widely used to explore the collective dynamics observed in active-matter systems. Although numerical simulations have revealed a variety of collective states, a general theoretical framework for the stability and bifurcations of the states remains unavailable. Here, by the model of one-dimensional ring-structured swarmalators with general distributions of natural frequencies and velocities, we conduct a systematic theoretical analysis of the stability and bifurcations of four representative collective states observed in simulations: the desynchronization state, the phase-wave state, the synchronization state, and the mixed state. We show that the macroscopic dynamics are governed by a low-dimensional invariant manifold, namely the generalized Ott--Antonsen manifold, and further establish that the same manifold underlies the collective dynamics of high-dimensional agent models, thereby unifying these seemingly different descriptions within a common reduction framework. Building on this connection, we derive stability conditions and bifurcation boundaries for the collective states and construct a bifurcation diagram in the two-parameter coupling plane, with theoretical predictions validated by large-scale numerical simulations. Our results clarify the dynamical origins of state selection in swarmalator systems and provide a theoretical foundation for analyzing nonequilibrium phase transitions in active-matter systems with coupled internal rhythms and spatial motions.

papers.title: From elementary processes to chaos: a discrete-time two-stage contagion model and its continuous limit
papers.abstract: Two-stage contagion, in which adoption requires two contacts with adopters, combined with population turnover produces bistability and relaxation oscillations, but no chaos, in Katriel's differential equations. From the elementary reactions, without reference to the differential equations, we derive a deterministic map $F_\tau$ for a large population updated in rounds of length $\tau$, as in elections, meetings or turns of a game: each individual makes at most one transition per round, events compete as exponential risks, and adoptions take effect from the next round. Katriel's equations are recovered as $\tau\to0$. Taking the probability $p$ of adoption after a single contact as bifurcation parameter, with rates and round length fixed, the map goes from extinction through a window of chaos to a stable equilibrium; for $\beta/\gamma=46$, $\mu/\gamma=0.002$, $\gamma\tau=5.5$ the window is $0.023\le p\le0.056$, bounded by the invasion threshold and by a boundary crisis beyond a subcritical Neimark--Sacker point. Chaos is supported by independent indicators: a positive Lyapunov exponent with Kaplan--Yorke dimension $1.81$, a matching correlation dimension, the 0-1 test ($K\approx1$ exactly in the window), a broadband spectrum, ordinal-pattern complexity, sensitive dependence on initial conditions and dense saddle periodic orbits. One-stage contagion, $p=0$ and permanent adoption showed no chaos. In the same window Katriel's equations have a periodic relaxation cycle: the round structure turns this oscillation into chaos and shrinks the oscillatory range in $p$ from $(0.022,0.41)$ to $(0.022,0.056)$. The chaos is thus a property of two-stage contagion with synchronous updating, not an artefact of discretisation.

papers.title: Exact Lyapunov spectra of affine cellular automata and the parity rule on networks
papers.abstract: The Lyapunov exponent quantifies the sensitivity of a dynamical system to perturbations, and the full Lyapunov spectrum extends this to every orthogonal direction in tangent space. For cellular automata the spectrum is almost always approximated numerically, and the approximation is delicate. We show that the affine rules, those whose update is an XOR of a subset of the inputs together with a constant, admit an exact Lyapunov spectrum. An affine rule has a configuration-independent Boolean Jacobian, so the spectrum reduces to the logarithms of the eigenvalue moduli of a single constant matrix, with no simulation and no limit involved. Two cases are shown to carry a closed form. For an affine cellular automaton on a periodic lattice the Jacobian is a multilevel circulant matrix, and its eigenvalues are given by the discrete Fourier transform of the rule's gradient stencil, valid in any spatial dimension. For the parity rule on an arbitrary graph the Jacobian is the adjacency matrix, plus the identity in the self-inclusive case, so the spectrum is the logarithm of the absolute spectrum of that matrix, and the maximal exponent the logarithm of its spectral radius. In both cases the exact spectra serve as benchmarks: they expose errors in previously reported spectra, and turn the informal correspondence between spectral radius and tangent-space sensitivity into an exact identity.
